items.title: Ecom 360 PME
items.problem: African retailers ran day-to-day operations on notebooks, spreadsheets, and improvised tills — cash errors, blind stock, forgotten customer credits, and end-of-day totals rebuilt by hand.
items.solution: Commerce platform with POS, real-time inventory, Wave & Orange Money on each sale, multi-store ops, and accountant-ready exports.
items.architecture: React SPA for POS and dashboards; Spring Boot multi-tenant REST API; async jobs for reports, bulk imports, and accounting exports; store-scoped inventory and role-based staff access.
items.security: TLS in transit, encrypted sensitive data, automatic backups, tenant isolation per merchant, and role-based permissions for cashiers vs managers.
items.scale: Multi-store chains with consolidated reporting; mobile-first UX for counter, warehouse, and field; stock decremented on every sale without manual recounts.
constraints: Reliable counter operations, even with unstable network conditions.
Strict multi-tenant isolation by merchant and store.
Traceability for sales, customer credit, and mobile money payments.
Accountant-ready exports for local reconciliation — not raw dumps.

decisions.title: Multi-tenant model
decisions.body: Centralize the platform while isolating operations, roles, and inventory per merchant.

decisions.title: Async jobs
decisions.body: Move exports, imports, and reports out of the checkout path to keep sales fast at the till.

items.tradeoffs: Operational robustness first — reliable checkout, tenant isolation, and reconciliable exports — over advanced analytics in v1.
items.bankingOutcome: Financial flows, local reconciliation, and multi-site ops with a minimum audit trail — patterns that transfer to FinTech delivery.
items.impact: 10+ merchants live across Senegal and West Africa; hours saved weekly on closing; Wave & Orange Money on every sale with accountant-ready exports.

items.title: Payment Platform Disaster Lab
items.problem: Happy-path payment APIs are easy. The hard cases start when a PSP times out (captured or not?), the client retries after an HTTP timeout, a webhook arrives three times, a Kafka consumer dies while events pile up, or a deploy breaks 20% of traffic — perceived availability and financial correctness diverge.
items.solution: Production / resilience engineering lab around a distributed payment platform: multi-service Spring Boot, dual PSP simulators, transactional outbox, and an SRE control center — proving no payment lost and none processed twice under partial failure.
items.architecture: API Gateway (JWT + correlation) → payment-service (state machine, idempotency, outbox) → dual PSP simulators with Resilience4j; Postgres per service, Kafka + Schema Registry; React control center to inject chaos and observe recovery.
items.security: Keycloak identity outside the business path; JWT at the gateway; X-Correlation-Id end-to-end; chaos admin endpoints scoped to PSP simulators.
items.scale: Isolated failure domains — kill a consumer or PSP A/B without collapsing financial invariants; outbox lag and circuit breakers as first-class signals.
constraints: Timeout PSP ≠ FAILED — uncertainty is IN_RECONCILIATION, not a reason to call PSP B.
Failover A→B only on certain failure (503 / CB OPEN / business refuse).
Never emit a Kafka event without committed payment state (transactional outbox).
Database-per-service so the append-only ledger schema stays isolated.
PSP simulators with hot-injectable chaos — not real Stripe network/SCA behavior.

decisions.title: Timeout = UNKNOWN
decisions.body: No blind failover on timeout; reconcile before truth — prevents double capture.

decisions.title: Transactional outbox
decisions.body: Payment commit and outbox write in one transaction so Kafka never lies about state.

items.tradeoffs: Correctness before “API always 200” — more payments in IN_RECONCILIATION and mandatory recon, in exchange for zero double capture on timeout.
items.bankingOutcome: Direct signal for payment platforms: distinguish certain PSP failure from uncertainty; idempotency, state machine, and reconciliation as first-class — not ops afterthoughts.
items.impact: P0–P2 delivered: Compose stack, payment-service with idempotency and outbox, dual PSP + safe failover vs IN_RECONCILIATION, SRE control center. Disaster scenarios D1–D10 documented.

items.title: Pan-African Payment SDK
items.problem: Products needed separate integrations for Orange Money, Wave, and Free Money — slow launches and inconsistent error handling across providers.
items.solution: One API for initiate, confirm, and reconcile — provider adapters behind a stable contract.
items.architecture: Adapter pattern with Spring Boot services, Redis idempotency keys, and Kafka events for async settlement notifications.
items.security: Signed requests, webhook HMAC validation, and per-tenant API keys with scoped permissions.
items.scale: Horizontally scaled stateless API; provider latency isolated via async queues without blocking client threads.
constraints: Heterogeneous provider APIs with inconsistent statuses and callbacks.
Retries must not create duplicate debits or duplicate notifications.
Shared observability across multiple payment corridors.

decisions.title: Unified contract
decisions.body: Expose a stable API while hiding Wave, Orange Money, and Free Money differences behind adapters.

decisions.title: Explicit idempotency
decisions.body: Treat every payment command with a stable business key to make retries safe.

items.tradeoffs: The adapter layer adds code, but it sharply reduces integration cost and provider-specific behavior drift.
items.bankingOutcome: Direct signal for banks and fintechs: unified Wave, Orange Money, and wallet integrations — patterns proven on ENG Technologie FinTech delivery and applicable to multi-provider banking corridors.
items.impact: Wave, Orange Money, and Free Money behind one contract — adapters and idempotency proven on ENG Technologie FinTech delivery. The packaged SDK is still being consolidated.

items.title: Double-Entry Ledger Platform
items.problem: Wallet and payment products need auditable money movement — balanced journals, safe retries, provider webhooks, and ops controls. A balances table plus ad-hoc updates fails compliance, idempotency, and reconciliation under load.
items.solution: Production-minded modular monolith for wallets and double-entry flows: balanced journal_entries, idempotent posting, transactional outbox to Kafka, maker/checker withdrawals, and operational freeze — with a live demo UI on the real API.
items.architecture: Maven modules (domain, persistence, core, platform) on Java 21 / Spring Boot 3.4; PostgreSQL + Flyway (append-only triggers); Redis rate limits; Kafka via outbox dispatcher; OpenAPI; Micrometer / optional OTLP.
items.security: JWT auth, webhook HMAC verification, RBAC (ADMIN / OPERATIONS / COMPLIANCE), Redis rate limiting, and DB triggers that block UPDATE/DELETE on journal_entries.
items.scale: Pessimistic account locking in deterministic order, scoped advisory locks for idempotency, scheduled reconciliation and balance snapshots — modular monolith boundaries ready to extract later.
constraints: Every movement is a balanced journal — DB triggers enforce append-only behavior.
Retries and duplicate provider refs must dedupe via idempotency keys inside the posting transaction.
Large withdrawals may require maker/checker approval before funds leave.
Demo faucet stays sandboxed — DEMO_MODE_ENABLED must be off outside local Compose.

decisions.title: Modular monolith
decisions.body: Split domain, persistence, application services, and HTTP adapter across Maven modules — clear boundaries without premature microservices.

decisions.title: Transactional outbox
decisions.body: Write outbox_messages in the same transaction as the post, then publish to Kafka via OutboxDispatcher.

items.tradeoffs: A modular monolith is easier to operate than split services, but module discipline must hold or the boundary erodes. Append-only + locking buys correctness at the cost of stricter concurrency rules on hot accounts.
items.bankingOutcome: Direct signal for fintech and payments teams: double-entry correctness, idempotent commands, webhook settlement, maker/checker, freeze controls, and observability — not a balances spreadsheet.
items.impact: Runnable Compose stack with seeded roles, live demo UI (transfer, merchant pay, withdraw, journal expand, trial balance, approvals), Swagger, Prometheus, and Grafana — reference platform for wallet and ledger delivery.

items.title: Unified API Gateway
items.problem: A multi-entity banking group and its partners needed one entry point to payment providers and internal services — without exposing fragile core systems. Patterns drawn from Synapse consultant delivery for Bank of Africa Group subsidiaries.
items.solution: Gateway for auth, routing, rate limits, and provider orchestration behind versioned REST APIs.
items.architecture: Spring Cloud Gateway + domain microservices; Kafka for domain events; Jasper/reporting decoupled from transactional path.
items.security: JWT at edge, RBAC, input validation before core contact, full request audit logging.
items.scale: Stateless gateway tier; Kafka absorbs analytics peaks without blocking payments.
constraints: Protect core systems while opening partner APIs.
Version contracts without breaking existing integrations.
Trace every sensitive request for support, audit, and compliance.

decisions.title: Gateway as boundary
decisions.body: Centralize authentication, rate limits, validation, and routing before any internal system contact.

decisions.title: Decoupled events
decisions.body: Publish business events outside the transactional path for reporting and observability.

items.tradeoffs: The gateway becomes a critical governance point; it needs discipline around versioning, monitoring, and access policies.
items.bankingOutcome: Aligned with multi-subsidiary banking delivery: API governance, core protection, flow auditability, and faster partner onboarding across group entities.
items.impact: Patterns from Synapse delivery for Bank of Africa Group subsidiaries: gateway as the boundary, versioned partner contracts, core systems kept off the public edge.

caseStudyPaymentDisasterLab.metaTitle: Payment Platform Disaster Lab — Case Study | Resilience Engineering | SAIFCORE
caseStudyPaymentDisasterLab.metaDescription: Resilience engineering lab for a distributed XOF payment platform — dual PSP, Kafka outbox, financial correctness under partial failure. Not a production PSP.
caseStudyPaymentDisasterLab.title: Payment Platform Disaster Lab
caseStudyPaymentDisasterLab.subtitle: Production / resilience engineering around a distributed payment platform (XOF, dual PSP, Kafka, ledger) — prove financial correctness when the system is not 100% available.
caseStudyPaymentDisasterLab.proofLine: Not a production PSP. A lab to show a payment system can stay financially correct under partial failures — no lost payment, none processed twice.
caseStudyPaymentDisasterLab.routingRule: PSP A down (503 / CB OPEN) → failover PSP B. PSP A timeout / UNKNOWN → IN_RECONCILIATION — never PSP B. Confusing D1 and D2 is a design flaw, not an ops detail.

metrics.label: Double capture on timeout
metrics.description: Uncertainty is first-class — timeout never triggers blind failover.

metrics.label: Disaster scenarios
metrics.description: Documented failure hypotheses from PSP down to deploy canaries.

metrics.label: Shipped today
metrics.description: Compose, payment SM, dual PSP + chaos, gateway JWT, SRE control center.

caseStudyPaymentDisasterLab.problem: Happy-path payment APIs are easy. Hard cases start when the PSP times out (captured or not?), the client retries after an HTTP timeout, a webhook arrives three times, a Kafka consumer dies while events pile up, or a deploy breaks 20% of traffic. Perceived high availability and financial correctness diverge — a blind failover to a second PSP can create a double debit; a non-idempotent retry can too.
caseStudyPaymentDisasterLab.solution: One directing rule: no payment lost, none processed twice — even when the system is not fully available. Invariant chain: Identity → Authorization → Idempotency → State Machine → PSP (uncertainty first-class) → Ledger → Event → Reconciliation → Observability. Timeout PSP ≠ FAILED; uncertainty is IN_RECONCILIATION, not an excuse to call PSP B.
constraints: Timeout PSP ≠ FAILED — uncertainty is a business state (IN_RECONCILIATION).
Failover A→B only on certain failure (503 / CB OPEN / business refuse).
Never emit Kafka without committed payment state (transactional outbox).
Database-per-service — isolate append-only ledger schema; no cross-DB joins.
PSP simulators with hot-injectable chaos — not real Stripe network/SCA behavior.
caseStudyPaymentDisasterLab.architecture: Multi-service Spring Boot (failure domains you can kill in isolation). API Gateway: JWT + /v1/payments + X-Correlation-Id. payment-service: create/GET, state machine, idempotency, transactional outbox. Dual psp-simulator A/B with Resilience4j — safe failover vs IN_RECONCILIATION. Compose: Postgres, Kafka, Schema Registry, Keycloak, Kafka UI. Frontend is an SRE control center (Vite + React), not a merchant checkout — observe, inject, recover.

decisions.title: Multi-services, not a monolith
decisions.body: Kill a consumer or a PSP in isolation — real failure domains for the lab.

decisions.title: Database-per-service
decisions.body: Isolate the append-only ledger schema; no cross-DB joins in the demo path.

decisions.title: Transactional outbox
decisions.body: Never publish a Kafka event without committed payment state.

decisions.title: Timeout PSP = UNKNOWN
decisions.body: No blind failover; reconcile before truth — prevents double capture.

decisions.title: Failover only on certain failure
decisions.body: 503 / CB OPEN / business refuse — not timeout or ambiguous 5xx.

decisions.title: JSON Schema + Schema Registry
decisions.body: Readable contracts in demos; CI-compatible evolution without Avro ceremony yet.

decisions.title: Keycloak + API Gateway
decisions.body: Identity / JWT off the business path so chaos stays about money movement.

decisions.title: PSP simulators + FE control center
decisions.body: Hot chaos via PUT /admin/chaos; frontend observes and recovers — not a checkout product.

caseStudyPaymentDisasterLab.tradeoffs: Correctness before “API always 200” means more IN_RECONCILIATION and mandatory recon. Split services + outbox buy isolation and Kafka replay at the cost of heavier local ops. One Postgres with logical DBs keeps the lab simple — not multi-instance HA. JSON Schema favors demo readability over Avro’s battle-tested evolution. Simulators give deterministic chaos, not real network/SCA/settlement. Canary/K8s land in later phases (P6); FE can run in simulation and risk diverging from real BE behavior until wired.
next: P3 — Ledger + Kafka consumers: double-entry append-only, idempotent consumer, DLT, Schema Registry end-to-end.
P4 — Notification + reconciliation: merchant webhooks; MATCHED / MISSING / DUPLICATE / AMOUNT_MISMATCH; poll PSP status out of IN_RECONCILIATION.
P5 — Observability: OTel traces gateway → payment → PSP → Kafka → ledger; KPI / SLO / CB / outbox lag dashboards.
P6 — Kubernetes + canary: Helm, probes, 5–20% canary, auto-rollback on error rate.
P7 — Documented chaos: fill D1–D10 (hypothesis → observed → recovery); wire FE to real backend.

caseStudyDoubleEntryLedger.metaTitle: Double-Entry Ledger Platform — Case Study | Fintech Ledger | SAIFCORE
caseStudyDoubleEntryLedger.metaDescription: Modular monolith for wallets and double-entry ledger flows — balanced journals, idempotent posting, Kafka outbox, maker/checker withdrawals. Java 21 · Spring Boot 3.4.
caseStudyDoubleEntryLedger.title: Double-Entry Ledger Platform
caseStudyDoubleEntryLedger.subtitle: A production-minded modular monolith for wallets and double-entry ledger flows in fintech and payments — balanced postings, idempotent commands, and a live demo on the real API.
caseStudyDoubleEntryLedger.proofLine: Not a balances spreadsheet. Runnable Compose stack with append-only journals, transactional outbox, maker/checker withdrawals, and a showcase UI that hits live endpoints.
caseStudyDoubleEntryLedger.routingRule: Every money movement is a balanced journal_entry set. Retries and duplicate provider refs dedupe via idempotency keys inside the posting transaction. DB triggers reject UPDATE/DELETE on the journal — corrections are new postings, never silent edits.

metrics.label: Journal
metrics.description: Flyway-backed triggers block UPDATE/DELETE on journal_entries.

metrics.label: Commands
metrics.description: Scoped advisory locks + idempotency keys inside posting transactions.

metrics.label: → Kafka
metrics.description: Events written with the post, then published by OutboxDispatcher.

caseStudyDoubleEntryLedger.problem: Wallet and payment products need auditable money movement under retries, webhooks, and ops pressure. Spreadsheet-style balances and destructive updates fail compliance. Without idempotency, a client timeout or duplicate provider callback creates double posts. Without an outbox, Kafka can advertise state that never committed.
caseStudyDoubleEntryLedger.solution: Modular monolith: domain, persistence, application services, and HTTP adapter as Maven modules. Product flows in PaymentApplicationService — P2P transfer, merchant payment (gross + platform fee), withdrawal (optional maker/checker), reversal, and deposit settlement from signed provider webhooks. Live demo UI at / exercises the real API.
constraints: Balanced postings only — account locking and negative-liability guards on the critical path.
Idempotency keys and provider refs must dedupe inside the posting transaction.
Above ledger.withdrawal.approval-threshold-minor, withdrawals return 202 + pending approval id.
Demo faucet (/api/v1/demo/**) gated by DEMO_MODE_ENABLED — never ship to production.
Webhook HMAC (WEBHOOK_HMAC_SECRET) required for provider deposit settlement.
caseStudyDoubleEntryLedger.architecture: ledger-domain (types/models) → ledger-persistence (JPA, Flyway) → ledger-core (posting, payments, wallet, outbox, reconciliation, webhook verification) → ledger-platform (Spring Boot packaging, REST, security, OpenAPI). Compose: PostgreSQL 16, Redis 7, Kafka, Prometheus, Grafana. Optional OTLP via Micrometer/OpenTelemetry.

decisions.title: Modular monolith, not microservices
decisions.body: Clear Maven boundaries without the ops tax of split deployables — extract later if needed.

decisions.title: Append-only journal at the DB
decisions.body: Triggers enforce immutability so application bugs cannot silently rewrite history.

decisions.title: Transactional outbox
decisions.body: outbox_messages and the post commit together; OutboxDispatcher publishes to Kafka.

decisions.title: Idempotency inside the transaction
decisions.body: Keys + scoped advisory locks so retries and duplicate provider refs cannot double-post.

decisions.title: Maker/checker for large withdrawals
decisions.body: Threshold in minor units; COMPLIANCE / OPERATIONS / ADMIN approve or reject.

decisions.title: Demo UI on the real API
decisions.body: Bundled static showcase with JWT login, faucet, transfers, journal expand, and call log — reviewers see real HTTP, not mocks.

caseStudyDoubleEntryLedger.tradeoffs: A modular monolith is simpler to run than split services, but module discipline must hold. Append-only + deterministic locking buys correctness at the cost of stricter concurrency on hot accounts. Demo mode accelerates review and must stay off outside sandboxes. Local Compose includes ZooKeeper for Kafka — fine for the lab, not the target production topology.
next: Product flows: P2P, merchant pay with fee split, withdraw, reverse, deposit settlement.
Ops: wallet/account freeze, trial balance, pending approvals, audit in the service layer.
Integrity: journal immutability triggers, deadlock-safe lock order, reconciliation + balance snapshot jobs.
Observability: Prometheus scrape, Grafana dashboard provisioned, optional OTLP export.
Tests: mvn test across modules; Testcontainers ITs when Docker is available.
